summary: 1935 CCC-built 110-foot steel tower in Mark Twain National Forest, Douglas County, Missouri; no longer used per the 2010 register entry; onX reports the cab restored with new flooring and stair work under way at a February 2026 visit; NHLR-registered 2010.

facts.design: 110-foot steel tower with a 7-by-7-foot cab, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps

access.note: The forest road to the tower (FS 121) has a closed gate about halfway up; onX says roads in the tower area are day-use only

visit.trail_note: onX says visitors can continue on foot uphill past the closed gate on FS 121. The sources read do not say whether the tower may be climbed.

notes_for_editor: Brief checked: county, agency and the 1935 build year match the NHLR. The 2026 condition and the Camp Willow company number come only from onX, a commercial trail-map page whose history section reports a February 2026 visit and a March 2026 documentation; treat it as secondary. The onX text says the cab and stair projects 'had since been completed' but describes the bottom stair flight as 'being re-constructed', so the story reports the stairs as in progress at the visit. The NHLR entry dates from 2010 and says the tower is in need of restoration; the story gives both dates. The 'unstaffed as of 2010' reading is inferred from 'No longer used'. The OpenStreetMap node (358066399) has no history and is not cited. No fire is named in any source read. Access is restricted by the closed gate and the day-use rule; no source says whether the tower may be climbed. No photos added.
